newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong troubles may limit stock rise - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong troubles may limit stock rise - brokers.

text.p: Rising liquidity in the market helped Seoul stocks open higher on Wednesday, but the financial troubles of Ssangyong Motor and the Jinro Group would limit any rise, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 1.41 points to 702.80 in the first 20 minutes of trading.
"The market appears to be solidly backed by rising customer deposits with securities houses," said Koh Kyong-bae, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
Ssangyong said it was considering selling buildings and land to raise 70 to 80 billion won to repay debts.
Analysts said Ssangyong's debts were estimated at 3.7 trillion won, while the company put them at 3.2 trillion won.
The automaker posted a net loss of 228.5 billion won in 1996 against 126.2 billion in 1995.
Jinro said on Monday it planned to sell real estate and unprofitable businesses including canned food lines by the end of 1998 to raise 1.2 trillion won.
Brokers said the restructuring plans highlighted problems of the two companies.
